subject: 🏃 Sunday — 14 mi Long Run w/ 5 @ MP (Wk 6)
html:
Tomorrow: 14-mile long run with a 5-mile MP fast-finish — your longest run of the V6 plan. Normal morning slot (Sonia's back), from the front door on the hilly home roads. HR governs everything.

First 9 mi easy: HR 140–155 (Z2–low Z3). Let pace float with the hills — your June 7 long run sat at 132–143 through the easy portion; same discipline. Last 5 mi @ MP: HR 150–160, target pace ~7:35–7:45 as a readout. This is your first MP block on hills, so climbs will push HR and slow pace, descents will do the reverse — govern by the HR band, not the pace number. HR ceiling 160; if a steep climb sends you above it, ease off and recover on the descent.

Pre-run activation (5 min): quadruped hip CARs · banded lateral walks · glute bridges · PT quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

Fueling (PF30, 60 g/hr — Week 6 cadence): 1 gel at T−5, then every 30 min (~30, ~60, ~90 min). Pre-load the ~90-min gel before the MP surge starts at mile 9 — the June 7 lesson was that a gel due mid-surge gets skipped. 4 gels = 120 g over ~2 hr = 60 g/hr.

Hydration (~2-hr self-supported run): ½ LMNT in your handheld (~500 mg sodium in 16–20 oz), drink every 15–20 min. You'll empty a single handheld well before the finish — plan your route to loop past home for a refill around mile 7–8, or carry a hydration vest. June mornings run cool, so 16 oz/hr is the floor.

Focus cue: Ease into the MP transition at mile 9 — don't launch it on an uphill. Find a flat or downhill stretch to settle into the effort, then let HR govern through the remaining hills. The terrain makes exact pace meaningless; the HR band is the whole workout.

Where you are: Week 6 of 12, Phase 2. 6 weeks to race day, 7 days to the Presidio HM pivot test. The solo-parenting week scrambled the schedule, but the knee has been 1/5 across every session — yesterday's stability landed clean (all Good), Friday's hilly run showed full recovery from the Jun 9 fatigue flag, and the two forced rest days mid-week leave you fresher than expected. Bank that freshness into the MP miles. Get to bed by 10, lay out gels and handheld tonight, eat a moderate carb dinner (rice + fish) — nothing heavy or unfamiliar.
